meta.dollars: constant 2024 dollars, CPI-U, on the same price base as the economics layer
meta.source: TEA Summarized PEIMS Actual Financial Data, fiscal 2009-2025

instruction_share.label: Share of the operating dollar reaching a classroom
instruction_share.question: Of every dollar spent on operations, how much is instruction?

instruction_ps.label: Instruction per student
instruction_ps.question: In today's dollars, what is actually spent on teaching each student?

debt_ps.label: Debt service per student
debt_ps.question: What is being paid on past building debt — money outside the operating total TEA reports?

security_ps.label: Security and monitoring per student
security_ps.question: What is spent keeping the campus safe?

operating_balance_ps.label: Operating revenue minus operating spending, per student
operating_balance_ps.question: Does the district's operating income cover its operating costs?

federal_ps.label: Federal revenue per student
federal_ps.question: How much of the budget is federal money — the part that ended?

limits: A trend describes a direction, not a cause. A falling instruction share can be a district cutting classrooms or a district opening them; this data cannot tell the two apart.
Operating balance compares operating revenue with operating spending only. Including debt service or capital would count buildings paid for out of bond proceeds as a deficit.

The shift between functions is real reallocation, not reclassification: the 16 function codes still sum to the reported operating total in every year, risers and fallers cancel to a zero residual, no single function absorbs the decline, and it predates COVID and continues after the federal money left. See meta.reclassification_check.
Districts under 500 students keep their series but are left out of the rankings: one retirement moves a small district's per-student figure more than a policy would.
Fiscal 2025 is the newest release and has had the least time to be corrected.

findings.headline: The classroom's share of the operating dollar has fallen for seventeen years
findings.detail: Instruction took 57.8% of every operating dollar in 2009 and 54.5% in 2025, a fall of 3.3 points. In constant dollars that is $369 less per student on teaching, while total spending per student rose. Re-derived on only the 1,142 districts reporting in both years, the fall is 3.2 points — so this is not a change in who reports.

findings.headline: Debt service is where the money went
findings.detail: Up 62% in constant dollars since 2009. None of it appears in TEA's operating total, so a district can look lean on instruction while carrying the state's heaviest debt.

findings.headline: Security spending has more than doubled
findings.detail: A 2.4-fold rise in constant dollars — the largest proportional increase of any function, and it comes out of the same operating dollar as instruction.

findings.headline: The federal money that masked it has gone
findings.detail: Federal revenue per student peaked in 2022 and is down 49% since, in constant dollars — back below where it started in 2009.

findings.headline: For the first time in seventeen years, Texas districts together spent more on operations than operating revenue brought in
findings.detail: 534 of 1,202 districts (44.4%) spent more on operations than operating revenue covered in 2025, and they enrol 67.7% of Texas students. The worst any earlier year in this window reached was 27.1%. Operating revenue against operating spending only: debt service and construction are excluded on both sides, and so is the debt tax levy that pays for them — otherwise a routine building year reads as a crisis.

findings.headline: The growth that used to pay for it has stopped
findings.detail: Texas districts added about 68,869 students a year through the 2010s. Over the last two years they added 25,614 in total. Debt service and fixed costs do not shrink when growth does.
